== united-kingdom/government-bond-yield
The UK 10-year gilt yield climbed to 5.38%, recovering from a three-week low recorded on October 15, as investors assessed stronger economic data and the outlook for interest rates and public finances. UK GDP unexpectedly expanded by 0.1% in August, avoiding forecasts of a contraction. The resilience has strengthened expectations that the Bank of England could raise rates, with markets largely anticipating a 25-basis-point increase on November 5, although those bets have eased slightly. Governor Andrew Bailey said there was limited evidence that higher energy costs were feeding into broader prices and wages, but cautioned that it remained too early to assess the risk of persistent inflation. Other policymakers, including Megan Greene and Huw Pill, have urged earlier action to prevent such second-round effects. Meanwhile, Chancellor John Healey is preparing his October 29 budget, promisin
The yield on United Kingdom 10Y Bond Yield rose to 5.40% on October 16, 2026, marking a 0.04 percentage points increase from the previous session. Over the past month, the yield has edged up by 0.17 points and is 0.87 points higher than a year ago, according to over-the-counter interbank yield quotes for this government bond maturity. == united-states/government-bond-yield
The US 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 5.12% on Friday, following an 11bps decline in the previous session, but remained down around 14bps for the week. Yields also stayed below the highs reached earlier this month, their highest levels since 2002. Investors continued to assess the Fed’s policy outlook, with comments from Chair Warsh at the IMF summit bolstering expectations that rates will remain unchanged this month. Warsh declined to signal whether another rate hike was under consideration, but said hotter-than-expected inflation had not altered his assessment of the US economy. Markets currently price in around an 85% probability of a rate hold in October, while assigning nearly a 77% chance of a 25bps hike in December. Markets have endured a turbulent week, with both US CPI and PPI data coming in hotter than expected, while a rotation away from AI-related trades prompted a broade
The yield on US 10 Year Note Bond Yield rose to 5.13% on October 16, 2026, marking a 0.06 percentage points increase from the previous session. Over the past month, the yield has edged up by 0.19 points and is 1.12 points higher than a year ago, according to over-the-counter interbank yield quotes for this government bond maturity.  Historically, the US 10 Year Treasury Note Yield reached an all time high of 15.82 in September of 1981. == united-kingdom/stock-market
The FTSE 100 recovered from earlier losses to finish higher on Friday, as gains in defence, consumer and energy stocks outweighed weakness in the banking sector. Submarine contractor Babcock rose more than 3%, while BAE Systems gained around 2.5%. Unilever advanced 1% and British American Tobacco climbed 2.3%, while Shell and BP each added approximately 0.8%. Mining stocks also strengthened, with Rio Tinto up 0.8% and Glencore gaining 1.7%. Banks remained under pressure amid reports that Chancellor John Healey plans to raise taxes on lenders in the upcoming budget. Lloyds Banking Group fell more than 1% after RBC Capital Markets downgraded the stock to sector-perform from outperform, while NatWest declined 1.7%. Pharmaceutical shares also lagged, with AstraZeneca down 2% and GSK losing 0.7%. The FTSE 100 gained around 3% over the week, following a 0.9% rise in the previous week.
United Kingdom's main stock market index, the GB100, rose to 10882 points on October 16, 2026, gaining 0.38% from the previous session. Over the past month, the index has climbed 0.61% and is up 16.33% compared to the same time last year, according to trading on a contract for difference (CFD) that tracks this benchmark index from United Kingdom.  Historically, the United Kingdom Stock Market Index (GB100) reached an all time high of 10991.07 in July of 2026. United Kingdom Stock Market Index (GB100) - data, forecasts, historical chart - was last updated on  October 16 of 2026.

== united-kingdom/currency
The British pound climbed to around $1.333 on Friday, its strongest level since September 22, after stronger-than-expected UK economic data reinforced expectations of a possible Bank of England rate increase next month. GDP grew 0.1% in August following July’s 0.4% expansion, beating forecasts of a contraction, while output rose 0.7% over the three months to August. The economy’s resilience has strengthened the case for tighter monetary policy, with markets still largely anticipating a 25-basis-point hike on November 5, although expectations have eased slightly. Governor Andrew Bailey said there was limited evidence that higher energy costs were feeding into wages and broader prices, but warned it was too early to assess the full impact.
